recommended_title: Verified Minimal-Investment Planning for Leaderboard Rank Targeting under Multiple Aggregation Rules
central_question: Under a declared per-task score-gain investment model, can a plan-verified planner find investments that make a target model strictly first on public multi-task leaderboards at a cost matching an evaluator-owned reference solver, across several aggregation rules, and how does it compare with naive investment baselines?
central_thesis: On the sealed final evaluation over Open LLM Leaderboard snapshots, a verifier-checked investment planner (selected on HELM MMLU v1.13.0) reached a qualified outcome: its mean efficiency relative to the reference solver was 1.0032, versus 0.8166 for the better of two naive baselines, with every plan well-formed; the evidence supports a narrow, conditional claim about planner cost-efficiency under the stated investment model, not a general or causal claim about real developer training or about which aggregation rule is most robust.
narrative_rationale: The grounded artifacts contain a completed, qualified final evaluation (final.qualification.outcome = qualified, status = completed, correct = true) with five metrics and two final seeds, plus a three-configuration search on HELM MMLU. They do NOT contain per-rule or per-target cost tables, so the original open question (how required investment varies with aggregation rule) cannot be answered with numbers from the artifacts. The strongest honest story is therefore a method-and-evaluation paper: formalize targeted investment (L1 point budget and L0 task count, caps, field, targets, success = strictly first), define the rule set, describe the verified planner and trusted verifier/reference/baselines protocol, and report efficiency relative to the reference with controls, while stating explicitly that rule-dependence of minimal cost is a hypothesis in the task contract and is not supported or refuted by retained metrics. Efficiency values slightly above 1 mean verified plans were on average marginally cheaper than the reference solver's (efficiency is capped at 2 per episode), so the reference is not claimed optimal and the planner is not claimed optimal either.
edit_framing_decision: Not in edit mode: no previous_paper directory or edit context exists. The framing is a fresh draft; the task brief's open-ended 'how does required investment vary by rule' question is retained as motivation, but the headline claim is narrowed to what the final evaluation measured.

method_groups.name: Verified minimal-investment planner (selected configuration: exact solvers for mean/median/maximin/plurality, verified heuristic or MILP level selection for trimmed/Borda/Copeland/z-score, plus verified boundary polishing and fallback)
method_groups.include_reason: This is the studied method: the frozen search winner whose sealed final evaluation is the central result.

method_groups.name: Naive investment baselines (uniform-gain and greedy marginal-cost; per case the better of the two)
method_groups.include_reason: The only baseline with a retained final metric (baseline_main_efficiency = 0.8166); needed for the comparison that qualified the run.

method_groups.name: Evaluator-owned reference solver
method_groups.include_reason: Defines the efficiency scale (episode efficiency = min(2, reference cost / verified plan cost)); readers cannot interpret 1.003 without it.

method_groups.name: Control conditions (permuted-input and within-task shuffled-score null)
method_groups.include_reason: control_efficiency (final 1.0002; search 0.9967) is the retained diagnostic that the planner is not exploiting input order; report with the caveat that the retained value is an aggregate and that candidate diagnostics are marked unverified.

method_groups.name: Search-stage configuration variants (basic solvers, +MILP level selection, +boundary polishing) on HELM MMLU v1.13.0
method_groups.include_reason: Three scored attempts (0 unscored) give a small incremental-component comparison: main efficiency 1.0031, 1.0031, 1.0051; the MILP layer yields identical combined score to the basic version, boundary polishing yields +0.0016 combined. Keep as an ablation, never as the main result, and keep separate from final results.

results_focus: Final (sealed, Open LLM Leaderboard snapshots, seeds 9001 and 9002): main efficiency 1.0032 vs naive-baseline 0.8166; control efficiency 1.0002; plan validity 1.0; qualified. Source ids: final.metric.main_efficiency, final.metric.baseline_main_efficiency, final.metric.control_efficiency, final.metric.plan_validity_rate, final.metric.combined_score, final.qualification.*, final.evidence.episodes.

Per-seed final episode scores (combined 1.00260 and 1.00257): the only variability evidence; report both values, state n=2 and that no confidence interval or significance test is available from the artifacts.

Search-stage component comparison on HELM MMLU (3 scored attempts, none unscored): main efficiency 1.0031 / 1.0031 / 1.0051, control 0.9967 / 0.9967 / 0.9967, validity 1.0; combined 1.00183 / 1.00183 / 1.00339. Report the +0.0016 gain from boundary polishing as small and unreplicated beyond 2 search seeds; the MILP layer showed no measured difference.

Search-to-final transfer: the selected configuration's main efficiency was 1.0051 on HELM search and 1.0032 on final boards; present as a descriptive observation, not as proof of generalization (different data, different boards).

Explicit scope statement: retained metrics contain no per-rule costs, so the claim that minimal required investment varies with aggregation rule is NOT evidenced here; list it as an untested hypothesis from the task contract and as the main limitation.
figure_plan: Overview schematic (page 1-2): leaderboard score matrix -> investment model (per-task gains, L1 point budget with cap, L0 task count with cap at field-best) -> aggregation rules -> planner -> trusted verifier -> efficiency relative to reference; shows target strictly first as success.
Final-evaluation comparison: grouped bars for planner vs naive baselines vs reference line (efficiency=1) on the final boards, with per-seed markers.

Search-stage component comparison: grouped bars of main and control efficiency for the three configuration variants on HELM MMLU, with y-axis zoomed and labeled to show that differences are in the third decimal.

figure_specs.purpose: Give immediate glance value for the problem: investment model, aggregation rules, planner/verifier pipeline, and how efficiency is defined relative to the reference solver.
figure_specs.layout_rationale: ICLR template is single-column with text width about 5.5 in; a left-to-right pipeline with 5-6 labeled boxes needs the full text width for legible 8-9 pt labels. Place on page 1 or 2.

figure_specs.purpose: Show final main efficiency of the planner against the naive-baseline score and the reference level of 1.0, plus control efficiency and plan validity, with per-seed values.
figure_specs.metric: efficiency relative to reference solver (main, control)
figure_specs.layout_rationale: Two small panels (main efficiency; control efficiency/validity) with at most 3 bars each fit comfortably at 0.8 of the single-column text width; labels stay at or above 8 pt without shrinking. Use only values present in paper_data (baseline value exists only for main efficiency; do not invent a baseline control value).

figure_specs.purpose: Ablation view of the three search-stage configuration variants on HELM MMLU, separate from final results.
figure_specs.layout_rationale: Three variants by two metrics fit one panel at 0.8 text width; zoomed y-axis with annotated values is required because differences are about 0.002-0.005. A small table is an acceptable alternative if the bars add no information.

supplementary_plan.purpose: Provide reimplementation-level detail and the full retained metric tables so the main text can stay focused on the qualified-final claim and its limits without hiding any evidence central to the thesis.

planned_subsections.heading: Investment model, field construction, targets and rule definitions
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Formal definitions from the task contract: independent per-task non-negative gains, no spillover, L1 cost with cap at 100, L0 cost with each task lifted at most to the field-best, field = top-K (K = min(N,200)) fully observed models by arithmetic mean, targets at mean-rank 2 and 10, strict-first success with ties against the target; rules mean, median, 20% trimmed mean, z-score mean, Borda, plurality, Copeland, maximin.

planned_subsections.heading: Efficiency metric, evaluator protocol and full metric tables
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Episode efficiency = min(2, ref cost / verified plan cost) with 0.01 cost floor, 1 for correct infeasible or empty plan, 0 for failures; main = mean over boards, cases, seeds; control = mean of permuted-input and shuffled-null efficiency; combined = 0.8 main + 0.2 control; qualification rule (main > baseline and replay reproduces). Tables of final metrics, per-seed episode scores and durations (31.4 s, 33.0 s), and search metrics for three variants (episode durations 9-37 s).

planned_subsections.heading: Planner components and verification procedure
planned_subsections.grounded_content: Description of per-rule solvers (exact for mean/median/maximin/plurality; verified heuristics or MILP level selection for trimmed/Borda/Copeland/z-score), exact-replica verification, pruning and fallback, and the boundary-polish stage (bisect shrink, drop redundant, pairwise transfer), taken from the retained program source.

planned_subsections.heading: Data provenance, snapshots and reproducibility checklist
planned_subsections.grounded_content: HELM MMLU v1.13.0 for search; Open LLM Leaderboard contents (sha 9c09a7ca..., 2025-03-20) and results (sha aa81ecc3..., 2025-03-15) for final; evaluator, program-tree and results-tree SHA-256 values from the final manifest; seeds 9001/9002 (final) and 11/12 (search); CPU-only runtime; license caveats; LLM usage statement.

forbidden_phrases: proves that the leaderboard is robust
notes_for_writer: Qualification: final.qualification.outcome = qualified, status = completed, correct = true. State this plainly and remind readers that qualification means main efficiency exceeded the naive baseline and integrity checks passed; it does not certify generalization beyond the final boards or real training effects.

Do not present per-rule required-investment numbers, rule-ranking claims, correlation-vs-shuffled-null results, or infeasibility counts: none are in paper_data. Frame the rule-dependence question as the motivating, still-open hypothesis and state that the retained evidence addresses planner cost-efficiency only. Missing diagnostics are unknown, not negative.

Efficiency >1 means plans were on average slightly cheaper than the reference solver's cost; per-episode efficiency is capped at 2. Do not describe the reference as optimal, and do not call the planner optimal. Differences between variants are in the third decimal with 2 seeds; do not call them significant. Seed-level spread is the only uncertainty reported (final combined 1.00260 / 1.00257; search c03 1.00339 / 1.00339 within about 2e-5).

candidate_diagnostics_trust is 'unverified' for all evaluations: note that retained control and validity diagnostics come from evaluator-side recomputation but candidate-reported diagnostics were not independently verified.

Keep search and final strictly separate: search = HELM MMLU v1.13.0 (3 scored attempts, 0 unscored, 3 configuration variants); final = sealed Open LLM Leaderboard boards. Do not claim an improvement over a baseline in the search stage (no search baseline metric is retained).

Use reader-facing terms: 'model variant' or 'configuration', 'seeded run'; call the metric 'efficiency relative to the reference solver' and 'plan validity rate'. If a threshold-based rate is needed, call it 'plan validity rate' only (fraction of episodes with a well-formed in-bounds response).

Page budget (ICLR, 8-9 body pages, no padding): spend space on (i) a rigorous problem formalization and investment-model justification with limitations (spillover, heterogeneous cost, field size K, cap policy), (ii) the rule set and why each rule is more or less sensitive to targeted gains in principle (mark as conceptual, not measured), (iii) planner and verification design, (iv) evaluation protocol including controls and qualification rule, (v) results, and (vi) a candid limitations section. If the grounded content cannot honestly fill 8 pages, shorten the claims rather than add filler.

References: references.bib currently holds only three on-topic voting-manipulation entries (Dey 2014, Yang 2014, Obraztsova 2011); the remaining entries are off-topic robust-statistics papers and must not be cited for support. Starter-literature items (MMLU, HELM, Benchmark Lottery, social-choice evaluation, Leaderboard Illusion, contamination work, Handbook of Computational Social Choice) are not in references.bib; cite them only if added to the bib with verified provenance, otherwise do not cite. Do not mention or search for the withheld prior paper.

Overview figure uses generate-concept-figure; other figures use matplotlib exporting PDF and PNG (300 DPI) from source, with the PDF referenced from LaTeX. If raster-only, at least 2400 px wide for full-width placement. Never upscale rasters.
Double-blind: no author names, repositories or self-identifying links; include an LLM Usage section (may be in appendix). Include the ICLR reproducibility/ethics statements as the template requires.
Title should name the mechanism and setting (verified minimal-investment planning, aggregation rules, public leaderboards) and must not imply a rule-ranking or superiority result.
